question: What is the primary aim of public health efforts in relation to communicable diseases?

options.A: To treat only chronic non-communicable illnesses
options.B: To protect and improve community health through organized efforts
options.C: To eliminate all microbial life from the environment
options.D: To focus exclusively on individual hospital-based care

explanation: Public health focuses on protecting and improving the health of entire communities through organized community efforts, health education, and disease prevention. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following is considered an epidemic-prone disease frequently encountered in Nigeria?
explanation: Lassa fever is one of the notable epidemic-prone diseases frequently encountered in the Nigerian healthcare context. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h1)

question: What are the three core elements that make up the epidemiological triangle?
explanation: The epidemiological triangle consists of three interactive elements: the agent, the host, and the environment. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h2)

question: In the chain of infection, what term describes the path by which an infectious agent leaves its reservoir?
explanation: The portal of exit is the path by which an infectious agent leaves the reservoir, such as respiratory secretions or blood. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which level of prevention is primarily focused on immunization and health education to prevent initial disease occurrence?
explanation: Primary prevention occurs before exposure and aims to prevent the initial occurrence of infection through measures like immunization and education. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of secondary prevention in communicable disease control?
explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early diagnosis and prompt treatment to halt disease progression and prevent complications. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of disease surveillance in public health?

options.A: To punish healthcare facilities for high infection rates
options.B: To systematically collect and analyze data to monitor trends and detect outbreaks
options.C: To replace standard patient clinical charting

explanation: Disease surveillance is the ongoing collection and analysis of health data to monitor trends, detect outbreaks early, and evaluate control measures. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why are certain communicable diseases classified as 'notifiable'?

options.A: Because patients must pay a special reporting fee
options.B: Because healthcare providers are legally required to report them to public health authorities
options.C: Because they only affect hospitalized patients
options.D: Because they do not require any medical intervention

explanation: Notifiable diseases are conditions that healthcare providers and facilities are legally required to report to public health authorities to track and control spread. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation separates infected individuals, while quarantine restricts healthy people who have been exposed.
options.B: Quarantine is used only in hospitals, while isolation is used only at home.
options.C: Isolation is for viral diseases, while quarantine is for bacterial infections.
options.D: There is no difference between the two terms.

explanation: Isolation separates infected persons to prevent transmission, whereas quarantine restricts movement of healthy individuals exposed to an agent during the incubation period. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which practice forms the foundation of standard precautions in healthcare settings?

options.A: Administering prophylactic antibiotics to all visitors
options.B: Consistent hand hygiene and appropriate use of PPE
options.C: Placing every patient in a private negative-pressure room

explanation: Standard precautions include consistent hand hygiene, appropriate use of personal protective equipment, and safe injection practices for all patient care. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the main mechanism of active immunization?

options.A: Injecting pre-formed antibodies for immediate temporary relief
options.B: Stimulating the host's immune system to produce its own antibodies and memory cells
options.C: Eliminating vectors from the surrounding environment

explanation: Active immunization uses antigens to stimulate the host's immune system to manufacture specific antibodies and memory cells against a pathogen. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is herd immunity?

options.A: Immunity acquired exclusively by farm animals
options.B: Protection of a population when a high percentage is immune, making disease spread unlikely
options.C: The complete absence of pathogens in a hospital ward

explanation: Herd immunity occurs when high population immunity makes person-to-person spread unlikely, protecting vulnerable non-immunized individuals. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following diseases is primarily linked to contaminated water and poor environmental sanitation?
explanation: Cholera is a waterborne disease primarily driven by contaminated water sources and inadequate sanitation infrastructure. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is an example of a personal protection measure used in vector control against malaria?
explanation: Long-lasting insecticide-treated bed nets (LLINs) are a primary personal protection measure used to prevent mosquito bites and malaria transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h7)

question: How is a disease outbreak defined?

options.A: When a single case of any infectious disease is diagnosed in a hospital
options.B: When observed cases exceed the normal expected frequency for a given time and place
options.C: When a disease is permanently endemic in a rural community
options.D: When laboratory equipment fails to detect microorganisms

explanation: An outbreak is defined as an increase in observed disease cases exceeding the normal expected frequency for that specific time, place, and population. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h8)

question: What is a primary objective of descriptive epidemiology during an outbreak investigation?

options.A: To manufacture new vaccines in a laboratory
options.B: To analyze data by time, place, and person to generate a hypothesis about the source
options.C: To punish individuals who failed to wash their hands

explanation: Descriptive epidemiology involves analyzing outbreak data by time, place, and person to generate hypotheses regarding the source and transmission of the disease. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h8)

question: What is the primary role of health promotion in communicable disease control?

options.A: To replace biomedical treatments entirely with herbs
options.B: To empower individuals and communities to increase control over and improve their health
options.C: To enforce mandatory fines for unhygienic practices
options.D: To restrict public access to healthcare facilities

explanation: Health promotion empowers individuals and communities to increase control over their health by addressing determinants of health and encouraging positive behaviors. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h9)

question: Why is cultural sensitivity important when designing community education campaigns in Nigeria?

options.A: It ensures that local beliefs, traditions, and language diversity are respected and messages are well-received.
options.B: It eliminates the need for any medical personnel in the field.
options.C: It guarantees that all community members will immediately become nurses.
options.D: It prevents the government from tracking disease statistics.

explanation: Cultural sensitivity ensures that health messages respect local traditions and language diversity, which fosters trust and improves community acceptance and participation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h9)
